chain.g: a workshop, art, trade, product of art, structure, fabric

ety.text: Borrowed from French fabrique, from Latin fabrica (“a workshop, art, trade, product of art, structure, fabric”), from faber (“artisan, workman”). Doublet of fabrica, borrowed from Latin, and forge, borrowed from Old French.

senses.d: An edifice or building.
ex: Anon out of the earth a fabric huge / Rose like an exhalation.

senses.d: The act of constructing, construction, fabrication.
ex: Tithe was received by the bishop […] for the fabric of the churches for the poor.

senses.d: The structure of anything, the manner in which the parts of a thing are united; workmanship, texture, make.
The physical material of a building.
ex: This church dates back to the 11th century, though the great majority of its fabric is fifteenth century or later.

senses.d: The framework underlying a structure.
ex: Only with the second actor, can plot, […] the reaction of man on man, be knit into the very fabric of dramatic art.

senses.d: A material made of fibers; especially, a woven one.
The texture of a cloth.
The appearance of crystalline grains in a rock.
The fired clay material of pottery artifacts.
Interconnected nodes that look like a textile fabric when diagrammed.
ex: The Internet is a fabric of computers connected by routers.

senses.d: To cover with fabric.
